goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and already take about 10% off City for Semenyo, and count City's 11 conceded in six. Guéhi has trained and Gvardiol is fit, so the centre-back crisis feared earlier in the week has eased; Khusanov and Nunes are still doubts, but a stand-in like Lewis or Reis is a small change, so I stay at 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners. City should have most of the ball at home after three defeats, while Fulham defend in a 4-2-3-1 and rely on Robinson and Castagne getting forward; Nunes possibly missing changes the right-back but not the pattern, so I stay at about 10.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, already counting referee Thomas Bramall (3.8 a game, below the 4.0 average) and Fulham's busier recent card count. No suspensions on either side and the stakes are ordinary ones for a Fulham side two points clear of the bottom three, so about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.8 shots, already adding about 6% to City for the shots Fulham have conceded lately. City react to a losing run at home with Haaland, Doku and Cherki expected to start, while Fulham have the league's thinnest scoring record; nothing here goes beyond what is counted, so I keep about 25.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target, with Semenyo's absence already counted. Haaland is fit and Fulham's front line (García, King, Iwobi, Bobb) is intact with King over his groin tightness, so I stay at about 8.8.

analyst_view.overall: City are third on 21 points but have lost their last three league games (Villa, Brighton, Forest), and Maresca has said there is no reason to panic while hinting at changes such as Bouaddi in midfield; Fulham are 15th under Alvaro Arbeloa, unbeaten in four league games but with only 10 league goals. City have won the last 20 meetings. Semenyo (knee) is City's only confirmed absentee and is counted; Guéhi trained this week after his hip problem and Gvardiol played for Croatia, while Khusanov and Matheus Nunes are doubts, which could mean Rico Lewis at right-back or a first league start for Vitor Reis. Fulham are missing only Cairney (knee) plus the long-term absentees Lecomte and Smith Rowe (counted), and King is over his groin tightness. Referee Thomas Bramall shows slightly fewer cards than average, which the numbers count; no morning news changes the picture from Friday.
